clinician.trajectory_summary: A 68-year-old man with type 2 diabetes and chronic HBV infection treated with adefovir dipivoxil (ADV) for 11 years was found with chronic kidney disease and treatment-resistant joint pain. Laboratory tests at admission revealed hyperphosphatasemia, hypophosphatemia, hypouricemia, increased fractional excretion of phosphate and uric acid, normal anion gap metabolic acidosis, elevated urinary β2-microglobulin, and glycosuria, indicating Fanconi syndrome. Bone scintigraphy showed multiple areas of increased uptake indicating pathological fractures due to hypophosphatemic osteomalacia. The 11-year ADV treatment was concluded as the main cause of Fanconi syndrome and osteomalacia.

Bone scintigraphy demonstrated multiple lesions with increased uptake indicative of pathological fractures from hypophosphatemic osteomalacia
